AAPL.rationale: Apple's fundamental health is genuinely strong: double-digit YoY revenue (+16.6%) and EPS (+21.8%) growth, expanding gross margins (~49.3% vs ~47.1% YoY), clean cash generation (OCF/NI ≈ 0.97x), and a materially improved balance sheet (equity up 59.5%, debt-to-equity down to 0.78x). The franchise is arguably the strongest in consumer technology with 2.35B active devices, ~90% iPhone retention, and Services scaling above $31B/quarter at ~76% gross margin. However, the market has already priced this quality aggressively: trailing P/E of 40x sits at the top of its 365-day range (30.5-43.1x), earnings yield of 2.5% is deeply below the 10-year Treasury at 4.57%, and the stock is at a 365-day high ($333.26 vs $334.68) after a +25.1% quarterly rally. The P/E has expanded ~23% over twelve months roughly matching EPS growth, leaving little margin for error. Near-term catalysts exist — Q3 FY2026 earnings on July 30 with consensus ~20% YoY EPS growth, China AI approval, and the $30B Broadcom deal — but these are partially priced in given the multiple expansion. KeyBanc's downgrade to Underweight (2026-07-16) flags that iPhone pricing increases could dampen demand and AI monetization is unproven. Regulatory risk to App Store commissions (worst-case 7-9% earnings impact) and rising component costs add downside optionality. The score reflects excellent fundamentals offset by a stretched valuation that demands continued perfection with no cushion.
